substantive_delta: The complete all-p deterministic quasipolynomial quadratic-log algorithm resolves the unchanged fourth-power original, with the full omniscient mask-dependent decrease-only adversary, zero queries, aspect-independent worst-execution operations and literal boundary cases. Relative to the verified primary Theorem 1.3 it extends p<=0.1 to every fixed p<1, reduces log^4 to log^2 and removes private leader randomness.
why_nonroutine: This is not obtained by substituting constants into the verified theorem. Its low-noise core and fixed quantiles do not certify center distances at majority corruption. A uniform unmarked-rectangle two-step bootstrap gives almost-full hidden seed cores at arbitrary fixed positive unmarked density and supports high quantiles. A different output construction charges compatible DFS leaf-path edges directly: one right exit per child interval and final degree two avoid the random leader degree loss. Retaining actual rather than worst-case outliers, with generated and singleton clusters counted separately, closes the quadratic weighted bound. The source hierarchy, future consistency, normalization and promotion architecture remain prior; overlap completeness and the final short accounting refinement are not separate innovations.
significance: The result gives a stronger complete algorithmic guarantee in a model whose nearest primary explicitly asks for computationally efficient polylogarithmic approximation. It removes the small-corruption restriction while approaching the unrestricted logarithmic benchmark to within one logarithm, and provides an abstract deterministic hidden-core extraction tool. This combined advance has substantive mathematical value even though competitive STOC breadth and technical depth remain unestablished. Novelty is assessed against the inspected primary results, not claimed as an exhaustive priority certificate.
